subject: Your reporting numbers come from a copy of your grants data
body:
Hello [First name],

 Leadership, funders and the government bodies you report to all want the same numbers: how many proposals went out, how many succeeded, how much risk sits in the grant portfolio, and how much funding income to expect next year.

Those numbers already exist in your costing system but the reports get built somewhere else, and your research administration team exports the grants data and loads it into a separate reporting tool such as Power BI.

The problem with that is the numbers are only as current as the last export, And a separate reporting tool can report only on what was recorded in the grants system in the first place, so reviewer details, early interest in a funding call, and line item cost detail cannot be reported on if they were never captured.
Futhermore, your team is still doing manual reporting months after the new grants system went live, which is the work the new system was bought to stop. And when your grants system cannot answer a question, people stop asking it, so the information drops out of your reporting altogether.

GrantsNow covers the whole research grants process, so reporting reads the live data in GrantsNow instead of a copy taken last week. The steps that used to go unrecorded are captured. If your team wants to keep using Power BI, they can, with GrantsNow feeding it the same data.

The whitepaper covers the rest: what gets recorded at each stage, what each role sees, and what changes for audit queries, funder requests and government returns.

campaign_name: GN_WP_8_Promo_Research 2 and 3 ("The Right Handover from Pre-Award to Finance")
body:
Hello $[UD:FIRST_NAME||]$,
Significant effort goes into agreeing the project cost base. But once those figures are re-entered into finance, the approved position can be lost, creating a disconnect between the original business case and the budget used to manage delivery.
1
Detailed costs get flattened
You build the budget cost by cost during the application. At handover, all that detail is squashed into a few broad finance categories, so no one can see how each figure was worked out.
2
The wrong number gets carried over
Sometimes the amount you asked for is used instead of the amount you were actually given. When that happens, the budget is wrong before the project even starts.
3
The same work gets done twice
Figures that were already calculated and approved during the application have to be typed in again by the research team after the award.
4
The problem keeps growing
Grant applications are up 57% since 2022 (Rees and Wilsdon, Nature, 2026). More applications lead to more awards, and every award still goes through this same slow, manual handover, so the workload keeps climbing.
GrantsNow carries your approved, contract-matched costing directly into the finance budget in one step, with each cost line already mapped to the right finance code. You enter your time inputs once, and the costing reaches finance intact.
Researchers at Institute of Cancer Research, Queen Margaret University and University of Portsmouth already use it. Because costing rules apply staff costs, overheads and funder rates as data is entered, costing accuracy improves by around 60% against a manual baseline, on the targets we calibrate against your own baseline.
